subject: Insurance
title: The Bhopal Gas Disaster
description: A 60-second lesson on The Bhopal Gas Disaster.

hook.text: In 1984, a pesticide plant in Bhopal, India leaked toxic gas, killing 16,000 people.

buildup.text: Methyl isocyanate gas drifted through slums near the plant. Residents woke choking. Thousands died in their sleep.

discovery.text: Union Carbide settled with India for $470 million—about $500 per victim. Critics called it insulting.

twist.text: Bhopal created global demand for environmental liability insurance.

climax.text: Bhopal's true cost was never fully insured. No policy can cover 16,000 deaths and decades of suffering.

punchline.text: 16,000 dead, $500 per victim. Some disasters are too enormous to insure.

quiz.question: What insurance lesson did Bhopal teach?
options: Industrial liability insurance became essential globally
